core_obligations: Separated case (proof lines 12042-12052): if U -> X is separated then it is quasi-finite, and the author shows that after restricting to a suitable constructible locally closed subscheme it becomes finite, using the standard criterion for finiteness of a quasi-finite separated morphism.

General case (proof lines 12052-12062): for an arbitrary etale U -> X the author reduces to the separated case by stratifying X so that U becomes separated over each stratum, which is possible because quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes admit finite partitions into locally closed pieces with good separation properties.
proof_roadmap: Treat the separated case using the criterion for finiteness of a quasi-finite morphism.
Reduce the general case by partitioning the base so that U becomes separated over each stratum.
Combine the two to get a single partition making U finite etale over each stratum.
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces a partition of a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme X into constructible locally closed subschemes over each of which a given etale morphism U -> X becomes finite etale (statement lines 12034-12040). The proof treats the separated case first, using the criterion for finiteness of a quasi-finite morphism after restricting the base (proof lines 12042-12052), and then reduces the general case by stratifying X so that U becomes separated over each stratum (proof lines 12052-12062). The non-formal content is the combination of the two stratifications into a single one. The claim is H2: two constructions, both written out.
